items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: And if Barney would kill him, Jimmy Hamilton would kill him. Kill him dead. ... Jimmy Hamilton, Barney. So, they splice him, the King of Swing.

ctx.x: Laid it on this turkey and the roof fell in. He stopped speaking to Fats, he stopped speaking to Duke. We killed him. This turkey walking around with Fletcher arrangements. Because that's where he got stopped. He bought Fletcher's book and we killed him. Killed this turkey dead. When that six brass showed up and them cats at the end, a "Cresendo" and "Dimenuendo" and start howling, Barly bar the door, man. He was a dead duck, man. You'd better believe it. That's the only time he ever run against him because we…

what was happening. He got proud, walking around, Benny Goodman. As a clarinet player, Barney would kill him. And if Barney would kill him, Jimmy Hamilton would kill him. Kill him dead. There you go. Stampede him man. It was one of those things. That was Chicago.

I was so busy. Chicago was a toddling town but windy. Man, wasn't no joint that I ever missed. Beautiful, beautiful. Ray Nance was playing down in the basement, in a bar, with Jimmy Noone that played clarinet, them cats and a guitar and a bass, them cats could play, man. That's the first time I saw him. What's that song, what's Jimmy's theme song? We play it, me and Brooks play it all the time. Clarinet thing. Man, Chicago was THE town.
